# <span id="aanchor283"></span> Liquid Cavern Editor

The Liquid Cavern Editor requires a Liquids Inventory Module license.

Liquid caverns can be added to locations to track total inventory and perform gain/loss calculations. Use the Liquid Cavern Editor to calculate inventory totals for liquid volumes.

<div class="procedure">

To access the Cavern Editor: Go to **Open** \> **Liquid Cavern Editor**.

When you create a new liquid cavern, a reference meter, along with either an injection or withdrawal point, must be specified before the meter can be saved.

- **Reference Meter** - A reference meter is required upon creation of a new cavern. The contract day and hour from the reference meter will be used to calculate the rollup IDs for cavern tickets.
- **Injection Point** - An existing station location specified as the inlet to the cavern.
- **Withdrawal Point** - An existing station location specified as the outlet to the cavern.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 645;height: 328;" />

</div>

## Cavern Configuration

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Cavern Status">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Cavern Status</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Cavern Status">

If a cavern is no longer active, you can change the cavern status to reflect this.

<div class="procedure">

To change the cavern status:

1.  Open the Cavern Editor.
2.  Select the **Configuration** radio button and click the **Characteristics** tab.
3.  Click **Edit Status**. The Location Characteristic Editor will open.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 396;height: 331;" />

</div>

Because location status can be datetime effective, users can specify the start and end times for which a cavern will fall under a particular status. This allows a cavern to be classified with different statuses over its lifetime. If the cavern level then changes on a cavern with a status of "Inactive", "Long-term Monitoring", or "Plugged and Abandoned", an exception will be generated.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Units Setup">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Liquid Cavern Units</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Units Setup">

User-defined liquid cavern units display on all Liquid Cavern tickets.

<div class="procedure">

To access and configure liquid cavern units:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Tank Editor**.

2.  Select the **Configuration** radio button.

3.  Click the **Units** tab.

4.  Use the drop-down menus to configure your unit settings.

    When units are not set or are left blank in the Liquid Cavern Editor, the units defined in System Settings are displayed in the Ticket Editor.

5.  Click the **Save** button.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 460;height: 192;" />

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Cavern Site">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Cavern Site Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Cavern Site">

Details about the liquid cavern site, including legal information and geographic details, are available on the Site tab in the Liquid Cavern Editor.

<div class="procedure">

To access cavern site information:

1.  Open the Liquid Cavern Editor.
2.  Select a liquid cavern.
3.  Select the **Configuration** radio button.
4.  Click the **Site** tab.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 534;height: 359;" />

</div>

The following data fields are available on the Site tab:

- **City** - Indicates the city the liquid cavern is in; up to 20 characters
- **County** - The county the liquid cavern is in; drop-down options are defined in the County Editor
- **State** - The state the liquid cavern is in; drop-down options are defined in the State Editor
- **Country** - The country the liquid cavern is in; drop-down options are defined in the Country Editor
- **Time Zone** - The time zone of the liquid cavern; drop-down options are defined in the Time Zone Editor
- **Section** - The basic unit of a township and range; each section refers to an area of a square mile; up to three characters
- **Quarter** - Each section is divided into quarter sections, which are each further divided into quarter sections, for a total of 16 parts per section; up to 25 characters
  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

  <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example">

  "NW 1/4 of the SE 1/4" refers to the most northwestern quarter of the southeastern quarter.

  

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 172;height: 171;" />

  </div>

  </div>
- **Township** - A measure of the distance north or south from the baseline, six miles in length; up to four characters
- **Range** - A measure of the distance east or west from the principal meridian, six miles in length; up to four characters
- **Meridian** - A geographical north to south reference point; up to 25 characters
- **Latitude** - A geographic coordinate specifying a north-south location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Equator; up to 12 characters
- **Longitude** - A geographic coordinate specifying an east-west location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Prime Meridian; up to 12 characters

</div>

## Cavern Inventory

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Inventory Level">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Liquid Cavern Inventory Levels</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Inventory Level">

You can manually enter an inventory level and FLOWCAL will use the specified volume and mass to initialize the cavern inventory level. The inventory level entered will be used from the effective date forward, and batches following will be added or subtracted from that level.

To set a cavern to a specific level:

1.  Open the Liquid Cavern Editor.
2.  Click the **Flow Data** radio button.
3.  Go to **Periodic** \> **New**.

Units for set level volume and mass are specified on the Units tab under the Configuration section.

</div>

## <span id="CavernTickets"></span>Reports & Tickets

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Inventory Reports">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Inventory Reports</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Inventory Reports">

Two reports are available from the Inventory menu on the Flow Data screen. These options will vary depending on whether you are on the Inventory tab or the Batch tab.

<div class="procedure">

To access the reports:

Go to **Inventory** \> **Print**.

If you're on the Inventory tab, a report displaying all set level records will be generated. If you're on the Batch tab, a report displaying all batches will be generated.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Inventory Empty">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Inventory Empty Tickets</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Inventory Empty">

Inventory Empty tickets zero out the volume, mass and component levels for the cavern. You can choose a date to run the inventory empty, and FLOWCAL will calculate the empty amount for GSV, NSV, Mass and Net Allowable per product and determine the gain/loss percentage. The percentage is calculated as:

GSV Percent gain/loss = GSV empty amount/((GSV in since last empty + GSV amount out since last empty)/2) \* 100.

An empty may be performed at the end of a batch accounted for within a cavern or a manual date may be specified. If a manual date is specified, you will be prompted to perform an advanced batch split. If the "Ignore Batch Split" option is enabled, the empty will be performed without splitting batches.

<div class="procedure">

To perform an inventory empty:

1.  Open the Liquid Cavern Editor.
2.  Go to **Periodic** \> **Inventory Empty**.

Double-clicking a record will open the [Ticket Details](../Tickets/Ticket%20Details/Ticket%20Details%20Editor.md) form; from there, you can view or edit ticket data as needed.

</div>

Inventory Empty tickets can only be generated through the inventory empty process and cannot be manually edited or deleted.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Product Conversion Ticket">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Product Conversion Tickets</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Product Conversion Ticket">

Product Conversion tickets can be used to convert the product accounted for within a cavern into a new product.

<div class="procedure">

To create a Product Conversion ticket:

1.  Open the Liquid Cavern Editor.
2.  Go to **Periodic** \> **Convert Product**.

You can select the product to convert from and the product to convert to and specify the relevant measurement data for both sides of the conversion. When saved, two associated tickets will be created to correct the volume, mass and components for each product.

Double-clicking a record will open the [Ticket Details](../Tickets/Ticket%20Details/Ticket%20Details%20Editor.md) form; from there, you can view or edit ticket data as needed.

Data must be rolled up for the cavern and its members before a conversion may be initiated. The product to convert from and to must also be set up in the Product Editor as a valid product conversion.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 560;height: 473;" />

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Table View">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Cavern Editor Table View</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Table View">

The Inventory tab in the Cavern Editor shows manually entered inventory levels, inventory empty tickets and product conversion tickets.

Double-click an Inventory Empty or a Product Conversion record to review ticket data in the Ticket Editor (see Tickets from the Cavern Inventory Editor). Double-click a Set Level record to view or edit an entry that was used to define the amount in storage at a given point in time. You can also specify the initial amount in a cavern.

Under the Batch tab in the Flow Data section, all of the batches from the meters in each injection and withdrawal location are displayed. The injection batches will add to the inventory; the withdrawal batches will decrease the inventory.

When a location is closed, the cavern inventory at that point is saved in the Closed Inventory columns of the database. Any edits made to a closed record are accounted for in the Adjusted Total Inventory columns.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 567;height: 225;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Info">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Info</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Info">

The Cavern Info screen allows users to configure information and import options for a cavern.

<div class="procedure">

To access the Cavern Info screen:

1.  Open the Liquid Cavern Editor.
2.  Select a cavern.
3.  Go to **Tools** \> **Info**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 585;height: 521;" />

</div>

The following options are available on the Info screen:

- **Fluid Phase** - The fluid phase of a cavern is always "Liquid".

- **Requires Close Approval** - Caverns that require close approval have to satisfy a set of conditions before they can be closed, and are closed manually in [Location Close Approval](../Locations/Close%20Approval/Close%20Approval.md).

- **Weekly Schedule** - This drop-down will list schedules created using the [Annual Schedule Editor](../Settings%20Manager/Application/Annual%20Schedule%20Editor.md). Location rollups will calculate totals for the cavern according to the date spans defined by the schedule selected here.

  Checking the Calculate Weekly Totals option in System Configuration will make the Weekly Schedule option visible for the locations, tanks, and caverns in that system.

- **Ticket Import** - Ticket import options are used to enable adjustment of ticket dates for daylight savings time or for time zone. When these options are enabled, dates on all cavern-level tickets that are imported into the location via TFX are adjusted. (See: [Date and Time Adjustments During Import](../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Date%20and%20Time%20Adjustments%20During%20Import.md))

- **Time Zone Shift** - When enabled, all dates and times are adjusted bu the offset amount defined for the selected time zone. (Time zones are created using the [Time Zone Editor](../Settings%20Manager/Geographic/Time%20Zone%20Editor.md).) For these purposes the time zone offset is to be user-configured based on the offset from the company's standard business time zone rather than offsets from UTC.

- **DST Shift** - When enabled, all dates and times occurring during daylight saving time are shifted forward one hour. All dates and times that occur outside of daylight saving time are imported.

- **Time Zone** - This read-only field displays the current time zone of the cavern.

</div>
